blocks.md: This lesson follows **Searching Beyond the First Trial** in *Adversarial Verification* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Adversarial Verification, § Searching Beyond the First Trial
blocks.md: A single successful fault trial demonstrates that the safety path can arrest the vehicle under one declared set of operating conditions. Physical machinery, however, rarely fails under tidy nominal conditions; subtle vulnerabilities hide in the narrow corners of the state space where timing jitter, payload shifts, and degraded surface traction align against the enforcer. Exhaustive testing across this continuous operational envelope is physically impossible, yet uniform random sampling requires an intractable number of runs to uncover rare edge-case failures.

questions.q: The section **Searching Beyond the First Trial** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Faults come from inverting each recorded design guarantee at its handoff and from working forward from the physical machine, each built as a five-element chain from cause to violated claim.
Signed temporal-logic robustness turns testing into an optimization that searches for the smallest margin, and a simulated margin counts only after its sim-to-real transfer discount.

Each fault record binds a signed header (trial, claim, envelope point, injection, oracle digest, latencies, margins, verdict) to the independently retained trace, carrying evidence and its gaps to release.
Kish's effective sample size of the importance weights and a tail-coverage check reveal when a few heavy weights carry the estimate.
